en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Latent Dispositions are Without an Object:
Are latent dispositions (anusaya) without an object? Yes.
Is form Nibbāna? Is the eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base Nibbāna?
One should not say so …pe….
Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust without an object?

Yes. Is sensual lust, the obsession by sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensual desire, the yoke of sensual desire, and the hindrance of covetousness for sensual pleasures without an object? [Yes.]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is sensual lust,
the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensual desire, the yoke of sensual desire, and the hindrance of ill-will toward sensual desire, all with an object? Yes.
Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust with an object?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust without an object?
“Yes.
“To which aggregate does it belong?
“It belongs to the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha).”
Is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) without an object (anārammaṇa)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object?
“Yes,” you say.
“Then should it not be said that the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness are without an object?”—
it should certainly not be so stated… [and so on].
Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust included within the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and without an object?
Yes.
Is sensual lust included within the aggregate of mental formations and without an object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is sensual lust included within the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and does it have an object? Yes.
Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and possessed of an object?

One should not say so… [and so on] … Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust included in the aggregate of mental formations and without an object, while sensual lust itself is included in the aggregate of mental formations and possessed of an object?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is it the case that one part of the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) has an object and another part has no object?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) has an object and another part is without an object?
Yes.

Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha), the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha), and the aggregate of consciousness (viññāṇakkhandha) has an object and another part is without an object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to aversion,

the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance without an object? Yes.

Is ignorance (avijjā) not-object (anārammaṇa)—ignorance as a flood, ignorance as a yoke, ignorance as a latent tendency, ignorance as an obsession, ignorance as a fetter, and ignorance as an hindrance?
One should certainly not say so... [and so on] ...
ignorance as a flood... [and so on].
Is ignorance, as an obstruction, possessed of an object?
Yes. Is the underlying tendency to ignorance possessed of an object? [Yes.]
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to ignorance without an object? Yes.
To which aggregate does it belong?
It belongs to the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha). Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object (anārammaṇa)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) without an object (anārammaṇa)? Yes.
Is the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness without an object?
One should not say so ... [and so on] ...
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance included within the aggregate of mental formations and without an object? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is ignorance included within the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and yet without an object (anārammaṇa)?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is ignorance included within the aggregate of formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*) and does it have an object (*sārammaṇa*)? Yes.
Is the underlying tendency of ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) included within the aggregate of formations and does it have an object?

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to ignorance included in the aggregate of volitional formations and without an object, while ignorance itself is included in the aggregate of volitional formations and with an object?
Yes.
Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) has an object and another part has no object?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of mental formations has an object and another part has no object?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is it the case that the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness are partly with an object and partly without an object?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it not to be said that “the underlying tendencies are without an object”?
Yes, it is.
Is it to be said that an ordinary person (puthujjana) has underlying tendencies (anusaya) while a wholesome or indeterminate consciousness is occurring?
Yes. Do those underlying tendencies have an object (ārammaṇa)?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Therefore, it follows that the underlying tendencies (anusaya) are without an object (anārammaṇa).
Is it to be said that an ordinary person (puthujjana), while a wholesome or indeterminate consciousness is occurring, possesses lust (sarāga)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does that lust have an object?
You should not say so… [and so on]… No, indeed.
Therefore, lust is indeed without an object.
The discussion on whether the underlying tendencies (anusaya) are without an object is concluded.
